title: Unique identifier in geofencing notification
description: The arrival/departure notification may contain unique identifiers (e.g., user ID, device ID) that can be used to link the notification to a specific individual.

title: Quasi-identifier through location and timing
description: Combination of location data (geofence entry/exit) and timestamp can serve as quasi-identifiers that may uniquely identify individuals when combined with other data sources.

title: Profiling through movement patterns
description: Repeated geofencing notifications can reveal movement patterns that enable profiling of an individual's habits, routines, and locations.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The system processes data that identifies individuals (arrival/departure notifications tied to specific users or devices).

title: Identifier in notification data
description: The notification likely contains unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., user ID, device identifier).

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location data (geofence entry/exit) and timing are revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject.

title: Observed communications
description: The notification communication itself can be observed by unauthorized parties, revealing that a geofence event occurred.

title: Sensitive location data type
description: Location data is considered highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected when strictly required.

title: Data propagation to external entity
description: Personal data is propagated to the external entity (EE1) where it may be accessible beyond the functional necessity of the geofencing system.

title: Data shared with external parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to external parties (EE1) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the geofencing functionality.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location data is being collected and transmitted when entering/exiting geofences.

title: Lack of control over data processing
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed and shared.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Location data may be processed beyond what is actually needed for the geofencing functionality.

title: Invalid consent for location tracking
description: Personal data collection and processing may not rely on valid consent from data subjects.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location history
description: Location history data stored in DS1 may contain unique identifiers (user IDs, device IDs) that can be used to link data records to specific individuals across different contexts or systems.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in location history
description: Location history data contains multiple attributes (timestamps, locations, routes) that can serve as quasi-identifiers. When combined, these attributes can uniquely identify individuals even without explicit identifiers.

title: Profiling individual through location patterns
description: Location history data can be analyzed to identify patterns in individual behavior, movements, and routines, enabling profiling that links data to specific individuals.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The system processes location history data which is identified personal data, directly linking to specific data subjects.

title: Revealing attributes in location data
description: Location history data contains revealing attributes (home address, workplace, frequent locations) that support identification of the data subject.

title: System response reveals location data existence
description: The map/history view served by P1 reveals that location data exists and is accessible, potentially exposing the existence of sensitive personal data.

title: Sensitive data type collected
description: Location history is highly sensitive personal data that should only be collected and processed when strictly required for the functional purpose.

title: Excessive amount of location data processed
description: Full location history may be processed beyond what is functionally needed for serving a map/history view, potentially including unnecessary historical data points.

title: Unnecessary treatment and analysis of location data
description: Location data may be further treated, analyzed, or enriched in ways not necessary to achieve the functionality of serving a map/history view.

title: Excessive duration/retention of location data
description: Location history may be stored longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risk through prolonged data availability.

title: Unawareness of location data processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their location history is being retrieved, processed, and displayed in the map/history view.

title: Lack of control over location data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their location data is processed, stored, and displayed.

title: Lack of control for rectification/erasure
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify incorrect location data or remove personal data that is no longer relevant.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: More location data is processed than is actually needed for the functional purpose of serving a map/history view.

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Location history data may be stored longer than needed, violating storage limitation requirements.

title: Linking through unique identifier in location data
description: Child's location data can be linked to the specific child through unique identifiers (e.g., device ID, user account), enabling tracking of the child's movements across contexts.

title: Quasi-identifier combining location with other attributes
description: Location data combined with other attributes (time, location type, family relationships) can serve as quasi-identifiers to uniquely identify the child.

title: Processing of identified location data
description: The Mobile App Backend processes identified location data of the child, which is personal data that directly identifies the child's whereabouts.

title: Sensitive location data shared
description: Live location data is highly sensitive personal data that should only be shared when strictly required. Sharing real-time location with a secondary guardian may exceed functional necessity.

title: Excessive location granularity
description: Live location data is disclosed at a very fine-grained level (real-time coordinates), which may be more detailed than functionally needed for guardian access.

title: Data propagation to external party
description: Location data is propagated to an external entity (Secondary Guardian) where it may not be strictly needed, increasing exposure risk.

title: Predetermined party data sharing
description: Location data is shared with a predetermined set of parties (secondary guardian), which is known at design time but still represents data exposure to external entities.

title: Child unawareness of location sharing
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating transparency requirements.

title: Lack of child control over location sharing
description: The child may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding who can access their live location data.

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Sharing live location data may process more personal data than actually needed, potentially violating GDPR data minimization principle.

title: Potential invalid consent for location sharing
description: Consent for sharing child's live location with secondary guardian may not be valid if not properly obtained, informed, or age-appropriate.

title: Location data linked to child identity
description: Live location data can be linked to a specific child through identifiers, enabling tracking and association with the data subject.

title: Location as revealing attribute
description: Live location is a revealing attribute that supports identification of the data subject and their movements.

title: Quasi-identifier combining in aggregated analytics
description: Aggregated usage and engagement analytics shared with advertising partner may contain combinations of attributes (e.g., device type, usage patterns, time spent) that can serve as quasi-identifiers, potentially allowing re-identification of individual users when combined with other data sources.
assumptions: Analytics partner may have access to additional data sources that could be combined with the shared analytics data.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on granularity of aggregation and partner's data access

title: Profiling through analytics data
description: Usage and engagement analytics can be analyzed to create user profiles, potentially linking data back to individuals through behavioral patterns and preferences inferred from aggregated data.
assumptions: Analytics partner has capability to perform profiling analysis on the shared data.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on partner's analytical capabilities

title: Quasi-identifiers in aggregated data
description: Aggregated analytics data may contain combinations of attributes that are unique to specific data subjects, enabling identification despite aggregation claims.
assumptions: The aggregation level may not be sufficient to prevent re-identification through quasi-identifier analysis.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on actual aggregation methodology

title: Data propagation to external analytics partner
description: Personal data is propagated to an external advertising/analytics partner where it may be accessible beyond the functional requirements of the app's free tier funding.
assumptions: The external partner may use the data for purposes beyond what is necessary for the app's functionality.
uncertainty_note: Confidence high - data flow explicitly to external entity

title: Data shared with predetermined external parties
description: Personal data is made accessible to a predetermined set of external parties (advertising/analytics partner) beyond what may be functionally necessary for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The advertising partner is a known, static recipient of the data.
uncertainty_note: Confidence high - flow description indicates external entity

title: User unawareness of data sharing with analytics partner
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their usage and engagement data is being shared with external advertising/analytics partners to fund the app's free tier.
assumptions: Privacy policies may not clearly communicate this data sharing, or users may not read/understand them.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on privacy policy transparency

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may lack control to set preferences or consent regarding how their usage data is shared with external analytics partners.
assumptions: No granular consent mechanism exists for data sharing with third-party analytics.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on app's consent implementation

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing aggregated usage and engagement analytics with external advertising partner may process more personal data than actually needed for the app's core functionality.
assumptions: The data sharing is not strictly necessary for the app's primary function.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on whether data sharing is essential for free tier funding

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing
description: Personal data collection and processing for sharing with advertising partners may not rely on valid, informed consent from data subjects.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may be bundled, pre-ticked, or not clearly specific to third-party data sharing.
uncertainty_note: Confidence moderate - depends on actual consent implementation
